findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same class body, so the second definition (line 152, taking a single `dimensions` string) silently replaces the first (taking `max_width, max_height`), and the first is dead code. Any code expecting either signature gets only the last definition; the dead first definition misleads maintainers and the Ruby interpreter gives no warning, so a future caller targeting the width/height signature receives the string signature instead and its second numeric argument is bound to `opts`.

[BUG] The signature change of `downsize`/`optimize` from positional `(width, height)` to a single `dimensions` string breaks every pre-existing in-tree caller that still passes two dimension arguments (e.g. animated thumbnail generation and `upload_creator`/`OptimizedImage` call sites that call `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)`). An old caller `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`; `opts[:allow_animation]` raises TypeError (100[:allow_animation] → no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) or produces instructions like `downsize 100` instead of `100x100`, so thumbnail generation of animated/normal images fails with a 500.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path as ImageMagick's input and output file, which the generated `convert` command cannot handle in place — the instructions are built as `convert <from> ... <to>` and ImageMagick opens/truncates the output before fully consuming certain inputs (notably animated GIFs after `coalesce`). Uploading a large animated GIF that needs downsizing runs `convert /tmp/x.gif ... /tmp/x.gif`; ImageMagick either errors (exitstatus != 0, `downsize` returns false which the caller ignores) or produces a truncated/blank file, which is then passed to `Upload.create_for` and fails or corrupts the upload; the loop can also never reduce size (non-shrinking `80%` of a PNG with large metadata), silently leaving the file oversized after 5 attempts with no error surfaced.

[BUG] The client hardcodes the max upload size to 10MB (`var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings`, while the server still enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. On any site configured with `max_image_size_kb` below 10240, a user uploading an image between the site setting and 10MB passes client validation, is downszed server-side to `80%` repeatedly, and the resulting file no longer matches what the user selected; if the setting is above 10MB users are incorrectly blocked client-side with a wrong limit message. The 413 branch at line 246 hardcodes 10MB for all upload types including composer attachments whose limits are per-type settings.

[ADVISORY] The API URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes` as the download cap, decoupling it from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, while the downsizing block below the download only runs `if tempfile && ... && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`. Admins who set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB get API URL downloads silently truncated/rejected at 10MB even though their setting allows more; conversely with the setting at 0 (unlimited) a 9MB animated GIF download is never downsized because the guard requires `> 0`, then fails upload creation with a confusing size error.

[BUG] The auto-downsize loop passes "80%" as the dimensions argument to OptimizedImage.downsize, which is not a WxH geometry string for the downsize code path. downsize_instructions expects dimensions to parse as width/height (e.g. via split on 'x'); "80%" produces garbage or invalid ImageMagick instructions, so large image uploads either fail the convert with a non-zero exit status (silently swallowed into upload of the still-oversized original) or produce a corrupt file instead of a downsized one.

[BUG] The class now defines downsize twice — the new three-argument def (from, to, dimensions, opts) completely overrides the four-argument def (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) declared four lines earlier. Any existing in-tree or plugin caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h) has its height argument land in the opts slot; the geometry becomes "#{w}x#{hash-like opts}" — every avatar/thumbnail downsize in the app silently computes broken dimensions, and the first definition is dead code.

[BUG] The client-side pre-upload size check hardcodes 10MB, replacing the per-type setting max_<type>_size_kb, with no matching change on the server side for non-image types. Administrators who set max_avatar_size_kb (or any non-image type's limit) below 10MB no longer get the client-side guard — oversized avatars/attachments are submitted, hit the server, and surface as a generic 413 instead of the friendly pre-upload alert; users also see a wrong 'max 10MB' message even when their site's limit is different.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes the maximum size at 10MB, decoupling the user-facing error text from the actual server-side SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. On a site with max_image_size_kb = 2048, a user whose 5MB upload is rejected with 413 is told the limit is 10MB — a factually wrong message that guarantees repeat failed uploads.

[ADVISORY] The animated-image branch of the downsize path is dead for this caller: the animation detection in optimize() tests from =~ /\.GIF$/i against the tempfile path, but tempfile paths are /tmp/discourse-upload-<type>-XXXX with no extension. Animated GIFs above the limit are downgraded through the static downsize_instructions path regardless of allow_animated_thumbnails, so the uploaded original loses animation even on sites where the admin enabled animated thumbnails — an edge case the diff's own allow_animation opt acknowledges but cannot trigger here.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop has no failure verification: after 5 attempts the file may still exceed max_image_size_kb, and each convert_with failure returns false without stopping the loop or being checked. A user uploads a stubbornly large image (e.g. a PNG that resists 80% quality reduction), the loop burns 5 ImageMagick subprocesses, then Upload.create_for is called with an over-limit tempfile anyway — the user gets a raw size error after a multi-second hang instead of a clear 'cannot reduce below limit' message.

[ADVISORY] The new auto-downsize behavior in the uploads controller, plus the refactored OptimizedImage.resize/downsize/optimize signatures, ship with no tests anywhere in the diff (no spec/test files added or modified). A regression in the geometry-string refactor ('80%' dimensions, the duplicate downsize def) would break every thumbnail generation and large-image upload silently, since no spec asserts downsize output dimensions or the controller's reduce-then-upload flow.

[BUG] The client hardcodes the size limit to 10MB, silently discarding the site's configured max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings. Users on sites configured with a limit other than 10MB see the wrong value in the 'file too large' alert and are client-side rejected/accepted inconsistently with what the server enforces; admins' settings become silently ineffective. This constant is not traceable to any stated requirement of 'downsize large images'.

[BUG] The 413 handler likewise hardcodes 10MB, showing users a limit that no longer matches the server's configured rejection threshold. When the web server returns 413 for a file over the actual nginx/Discourse limit, the user is told the limit is 10MB regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, producing a false error message.

[BUG] The API-URL download path silently replaces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap. API uploads via URL bypass the site's configured download size limit — a site configured for 2MB will happily download 10MB images, and a site configured for 50MB will truncate at 10MB, both contradicting the stated feature scope of 'downsizing large images'.

[BUG] Ruby syntax error: the file defines `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then redefines `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` with a different arity — the second definition overrides the first, so every existing call site passing width and height as separate arguments (e.g. downsize(path, path, 100, 100)) now passes 100 as `dimensions` and 100 as `opts`, raising ArgumentError/TypeError. All existing OptimizedImage.downsize callers (thumbnail/cooked-image generation) break at runtime because the 4-arg signature no longer matches the new 3-arg+opts signature; this is a syntax-level redefinition the diff introduced.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%') — an in-place operation on a tempfile with a non-image-extension path, and the animated-instruction branch keys off `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, which can never match a random tempfile name. Animated GIFs uploaded via this path never take the animated instructions and lose frames/coalesce behavior; the '80%' quality-reduction loop may also fail to converge within 5 attempts for large files, silently passing an over-limit tempfile to Upload.create_for which then errors — the 'automatic downsizing' invariant the feature promises is not actually enforced.

[ADVISORY] Fixed 5-attempt loop with a hardcoded '80%' quality step is untraceable to any requirement and provides no guarantee the result is under the limit. Uploaders of e.g. a 40MB PNG on a 1MB-limit site get 5 rounds of downsizing and then a failure anyway, wasting CPU on convert calls; the loop bound and quality factor are magic numbers with no setting or rationale.

[BUG] The diff defines `self.downsize` twice in the same module: the first (4-arg, width/height) and the second (dimensions-string) — in Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so every existing caller that invokes downsize with separate width/height arguments now hits the 4-parameter definition and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 4). Any existing code path calling OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) — e.g. thumbnail generation elsewhere in the codebase — crashes with ArgumentError instead of producing a resized image; the resize call sites outside this diff were never updated to the new dimensions-string signature.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes the same path as both input and output (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`), and ImageMagick's convert cannot safely read and write the same file in one invocation — the output file is truncated/corrupted mid-read, producing a zero-byte or garbage tempfile that is then handed to Upload.create_for. Users uploading large images get corrupted uploads (or failures that surface as opaque errors) instead of a downsized image; the re-upload path replaces the user's original file content with garbage.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size check is hardcoded to 10MB instead of reading SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, decoupling the client gate from the server's configurable limit. Admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10MB have valid uploads blocked client-side with a wrong 'max size' message; admins who lower it get no client feedback, and the 413 handler (line ~246) now reports 10MB regardless of the actual server limit, misleading users on every rejected upload.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs at most 5 iterations of 80% scaling with no convergence check: five 80% reductions only shrink a file ~3.3x, so a sufficiently large image (e.g. 40MB vs a 2MB limit) still exceeds max_image_size_kb after the loop, yet Upload.create_for is called anyway. Users uploading very large images hit the server-side size validation after the CPU cost of five ImageMagick invocations, and the hard cap of 5 is a magic constant that silently fails for inputs it cannot converge on, instead of computing the correct scale factor once from the actual size delta.

[ADVISORY] Using OptimizedImage (a model for cached thumbnail generation) as the entry point for mutating user upload tempfiles conflates two ownership boundaries — upload processing now depends on the thumbnail subsystem's class methods, so any refactor of thumbnail generation (e.g. changing `optimize`'s signature again, as this very diff does) breaks the upload path. The next maintainer who changes OptimizedImage's methods for thumbnail needs has no signal that uploads_controller's image-reduction step also depends on them; this diff's own duplicate-definition breakage in optimized_image.rb is a direct instance of that coupling.

[BUG] The client-side upload size check discards the per-site configurable limit (SiteSetting max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb) and hardcodes 10MB, silently removing operator configuration that the feature was supposed to respect. Admins who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB see users upload oversized images that are then server-side downsized or rejected inconsistently; admins who set it above 10MB see legitimate uploads blocked at 10MB with no setting to change it — the accepted constraint (site-configurable limits) was replaced without any setting or migration.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB instead of the server's actual SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message no longer reflects the real limit the server enforces. Users who hit a 413 from a server configured with a different limit (e.g. 2MB) get a message telling them 10MB is the max, then hit the same 413 again when they retry with a file under 10MB but over the real limit.

[BUG] The API URL-download size cap was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, decoupling it from the operator's configured limit. Operators relying on max_image_size_kb to bound remote-download memory/disk usage lose that control; API-triggered downloads now fetch files up to 10MB regardless of the site setting, silently changing the accepted resource-limit contract.

[BUG] The new downsize loop overwrites the user's original uploaded file in place (tempfile.path as both source and destination) before Upload.create_for, so the stored upload is the lossy re-encoded image rather than the original. Users who upload a large image lose the original full-resolution data permanently — the PR's stated intent is 'downsize large images' for compliance, but the artifact also destroys the original for every oversized image, including animated GIFs re-encoded under allow_animated_thumbnails, with no retention of the unmodified source.

[BUG] The class now defines def self.downsize twice (the 4-argument version then the 3-argument version), so the later definition silently replaces the former and all existing callers that pass (from, to, max_width, max_height) now hit the 3-parameter method and raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Every pre-existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize with width/height arguments (e.g. thumbnail generation paths) crashes with ArgumentError, breaking image optimization site-wide, not just the new upload path.

[BUG] The downsize loop caps at 5 attempts and does not verify the file is under the limit before calling Upload.create_for, so an image ImageMagick fails to shrink (convert error, or a dimension-heavy image whose '80%' downsize barely reduces bytes) passes through still over SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. A user uploads an image that survives 5 downsizing attempts above the configured limit; the upload is created anyway, bypassing the server-side size policy the setting exists to enforce (and any per-type max enforced downstream keys off tempfile.size which is now attacker-influenced).

[ADVISORY] Each upload can trigger up to five synchronous ImageMagick conversions of a user-supplied file inside the request cycle, with no file-format/animation guard beyond allow_animated_thumbnails. Any logged-in user can submit a pathologically expensive image (e.g. a 10MB animated GIF or a huge-dimension image) and force the server to run 5 full conversions per upload in-request, multiplying CPU/latency cost and enabling cheap resource-exhaustion of worker processes.

[ADVISORY] After the downsize loop rewrites the tempfile via ImageMagick, the original client-supplied content_type is still passed to Upload.create_for, and the downsize result (success or failure) is not checked. A mismatched/spoofed content_type survives the transformation, so the stored upload's declared type reflects client input rather than the post-conversion file's actual type, weakening any downstream type-based handling of the re-encoded image.

[ADVISORY] The client-side upload size check replaces the admin-configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb (and max_attachment_size_kb) with a hardcoded 10MB, so the pre-flight gate no longer reflects the server's configured policy. On sites with a limit below 10MB users are told 10MB is acceptable and hit a server rejection after a full upload; on sites allowing more than 10MB users are wrongly blocked — the trust boundary check is now hardcoded rather than policy-driven, guaranteeing client/server drift.

[BUG] self.downsize is defined twice in the same module body (4-arg form then 3-arg form), so the second definition silently overrides the first and the width/height-based signature is dead code. Any existing caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) now hits the 3-positional-arg definition and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and the duplicate definition masks the fact that the two signatures were intended to coexist; the first definition is unreachable and any test exercising the 4-arg form would fail with an exception rather than exercising resize semantics.

[BUG] The signature of the public method self.downsize changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), collapsing two dimensional arguments into one, with no caller updates or test updates in this diff. Pre-existing call sites and any existing specs that pass width and height separately now pass the height value as the opts hash position (or raise ArgumentError), so stale tests either fail with the wrong-shaped instructions or no longer exercise the real downsize geometry — the diff changed the method's contract without any test verifying the new 'WxH' string format (e.g. that downsize_instructions receives '80%' verbatim and builds the correct convert command).

[ADVISORY] The new downsize-retry loop in create_upload passes allow_animation via OptimizedImage.downsize, whose animated branch is selected by a regex on the from path (from =~ /\.GIF$/i) — the in-place tempfile path 'discourse-upload-<type>' has an extension derived from the original filename, but the loop re-runs on the mutated file, and no test in the diff exercises either the animated or the non-shrinking case. Operators uploading an animated GIF larger than max_image_size_kb trigger up to 5 full convert passes that may either preserve animation (allow_animated_thumbnails) or strip frames; a regression here (wrong instructions string, 0-byte output after in-place overwrite when convert fails mid-write) destroys the user's upload bytes in place before Upload.create_for ever runs, and no spec in this diff pins the instruction-building or the loop bound.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size gate now hardcodes 10 * 1024 KB for every upload type, replacing the per-type SiteSetting lookup, and no test change in this diff verifies the new client limit or the server-side guarantee that images above max_image_size_kb are downgraded rather than rejected. For any non-image file type (or an image the server cannot shrink further, e.g. already tiny dimensions but large bytes), the client tells users 10MB is allowed while the server still rejects at max_image_size_kb, producing a misleading error; the client/server contract change is unverified, and the 413 path's new hardcoded 10MB message can contradict the actual server setting shown in the same dialog.

[BUG] The automatic downsize loop gives up after 5 attempts and then calls Upload.create_for with the still-too-large tempfile, so the upload fails with a generic file_too_large error instead of ever succeeding. A user uploads a 40MB image on a site with max_image_size_kb=1024: five 80% downsizes leave it above 1MB (0.8^5 ≈ 33%), and Upload.create_for rejects it — the advertised feature (large images automatically reduced) silently does not work for exactly the large files it targets.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both from and to (in-place), and convert_with shells out to ImageMagick which requires distinct input/output files, so the downsize either fails (exitstatus != 0, loop spins 5 times doing nothing) or clobbers the input. Every large-image upload hits a failing convert (or a zeroed/corrupted tempfile), then Upload.create_for is handed a corrupt/oversized file; users uploading images over the limit get broken uploads instead of downsized ones.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in the same class body — the second def (line 148) redefines and shadows the first (line 142), so the width/height-arity variant is dead code and any caller relying on it gets the dimensions-string version instead. The next reader/maintainer edits the first definition believing it is live; existing callers passing max_width, max_height positionally now hit the second definition where height is bound to opts and the geometry string is built from nil ('1000x'), producing broken convert commands.

[ADVISORY] resize/downsize/optimize changed from (width, height) parameters to a single dimensions string, but only in-model call sites are updated in this diff — out-of-tree or unshown callers passing two arguments break with ArgumentError (extra arg) or produce wrong geometry. Any plugin or code path still calling OptimizedImage.resize(from, to, 100, 75) crashes at deploy time; the signature change is a silent public-surface break with no deprecation shim.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size check was hardcoded to 10MB, decoupling it from SiteSetting max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb, so the client no longer tells the truth about server limits. On sites with max_attachment_size_kb = 512, users are told 10MB is fine client-side, upload a 5MB attachment (not an image, so the new downsize path doesn't help), and get a server-side 413 after a full 5MB upload — wasted bandwidth and a confusing error for every operator whose settings differ from 10MB.

[ADVISORY] FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs is now capped at a hardcoded 10.megabytes, ignoring SiteSetting, so URLs larger than 10MB fail even on sites whose max_image_size_kb permits more, and the hardcoded cap silently overrides operator configuration. Admin on a site with max_image_size_kb = 20480 who POSTs an API upload with a 12MB image URL gets a failed download and a nil tempfile, where the old code honored their setting.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop passes '80%' as the dimensions argument into downsize_instructions (and downsize_instructions_animated), which expect a WxH geometry string; a percentage geometry changes semantics from 'fit within box' to 'scale to 80% of original', so oversized-but-small-dimension images (e.g. a 300x200 PNG at 8MB) are scaled down needlessly while still failing the size check. Users with dense PNGs get progressively degraded image quality (80% each iteration) with no guarantee of passing the limit, and animated-GIF handling via downsize_instructions_animated receives a geometry its thumbnail/w/h parsing does not expect, risking convert failures on exactly the animated images allow_animated_thumbnails is meant to preserve.

[BUG] The public downsize method's signature was changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), so every existing caller that passes width and height as two separate arguments now produces a broken command. Any out-of-diff call site like OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100) now passes the integer 100 where a geometry string is expected, so downsize_instructions builds an ImageMagick command with a malformed geometry (or nil.to_s interpolation), convert_with fails or produces a zero-byte file, and thumbnail/avatar generation breaks with exitstatus != 0 that the caller may not handle — a runtime failure on every pre-existing thumbnail path touched by this signature change.

[BUG] downsize is defined twice in the same module — the second definition (line 151) silently replaces the first (line 142), and both are identical, indicating a botched edit that hides which definition is live. Future maintainers editing the first definition see no effect, and any subtle divergence between the two bodies would silently choose the wrong behavior; the duplicate is dead code that degrades change-safety of the very function this feature depends on.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value (false on ImageMagick failure) and retries blindly, then falls through to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized file when all 5 attempts fail. A user uploading a large or corrupt image that ImageMagick cannot shrink gets five wasted shell invocations (each spawning a full convert of the oversized file, a hot-path cost on the request thread) followed by a generic 'file too large' error with no indication downsizing was attempted and failed; the silent-partial promise of this feature ('large images are automatically reduced') is broken with no log of the convert failure.

[ADVISORY] Five successive '80%' downsizes shrink the image to at most ~33% of its original size, so any image over ~3x the limit exhausts the loop and the upload proceeds oversized. A user uploading a 30MB image against a 3MB site limit ends at ~9.8MB after five passes, and the request then fails with the size error — the auto-downsize feature silently doesn't work for exactly the large files it was built for, with no server-side signal distinguishing 'downsizing worked' from 'gave up'.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with in-place input/output (tempfile.path as both from and to) via a shell backtick, and ImageMagick reading and writing the same path can truncate the file on failure or partial write, leaving a corrupt tempfile that is then passed to Upload.create_for. When a convert invocation fails mid-write (disk full, OOM on a huge image), the original upload bytes are destroyed in place, so the retry loop operates on a corrupted file and the user gets a confusing parse/upload error rather than the original file being validated or rejected intact.

[ADVISORY] The client-side max size check is hardcoded to 10MB, decoupled from the server's SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb that the server still enforces. On sites configured with max_image_size_kb above 10MB (or unlimited), users are blocked client-side with a 'file too large' bootbox citing a 10MB limit the server does not actually impose for images that this feature would downsize anyway; on sites below 10MB the client lets oversized files through and the user gets the server error — the client message is wrong in both directions because the guard it replaced was the single source of truth.

[ADVISORY] The image test uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) where filename is derived from the URL basename for API URL uploads, so an image-served-under-a-non-image-name (e.g. '.../get?format=png' or a redirect URL with no extension) is not downsized even though its bytes are an image. API users pasting such URLs hit the raw size limit and get a too-large error despite the feature's promise, while the byte-level content (and content_type, available for the file branch) is never consulted; the skip is silent — no log, no distinguishing error.

[BUG] The signature change of `downsize`/`optimize` from positional `(width, height)` to a single `dimensions` string breaks every pre-existing in-tree caller that still passes two dimension arguments (e.g. animated thumbnail generation and `upload_creator`/`OptimizedImage` call sites that call `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)`). An old caller `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`; `opts[:allow_animation]` raises TypeError (100[:allow_animation] → no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) or produces instructions like `downsize 100` instead of `100x100`, so thumbnail generation of animated/normal images fails with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` is defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later redefined as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the latter overrides the former, so any existing caller still passing `(max_width, max_height)` will bind `dimensions=max_width` and `opts=max_height` (likely an Integer), causing `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` to raise a `TypeError` and/or generating invalid resize instructions. This is a runtime-breaking API change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path as ImageMagick's input and output file, which the generated `convert` command cannot handle in place — the instructions are built as `convert <from> ... <to>` and ImageMagick opens/truncates the output before fully consuming certain inputs (notably animated GIFs after `coalesce`). Uploading a large animated GIF that needs downsizing runs `convert /tmp/x.gif ... /tmp/x.gif`; ImageMagick either errors (exitstatus != 0, `downsize` returns false which the caller ignores) or produces a truncated/blank file, which is then passed to `Upload.create_for` and fails or corrupts the upload; the loop can also never reduce size (non-shrinking `80%` of a PNG with large metadata), silently leaving the file oversized after 5 attempts with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. the same filesystem path is used for both the input (`from`) and output (`to`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` passes both `from` and `to` to `*_instructions` and then executes the resulting ImageMagick command via `convert_with(instructions, to)`, which strongly implies a `convert <from> ... <to>` style invocation. In-place conversion is a known failure mode for ImageMagick in many cases, and the diff also shows the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored inside the loop, so a failed/partial conversion would not be detected before proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the (potentially corrupted/unchanged) tempfile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client hardcodes the max upload size to 10MB (`var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings`, while the server still enforces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. On any site configured with `max_image_size_kb` below 10240, a user uploading an image between the site setting and 10MB passes client validation, is downszed server-side to `80%` repeatedly, and the resulting file no longer matches what the user selected; if the setting is above 10MB users are incorrectly blocked client-side with a wrong limit message. The 413 branch at line 246 hardcodes 10MB for all upload types including composer attachments whose limits are per-type settings.

[ADVISORY] The API URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes` as the download cap, decoupling it from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, while the downsizing block below the download only runs `if tempfile && ... && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`. Admins who set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB get API URL downloads silently truncated/rejected at 10MB even though their setting allows more; conversely with the setting at 0 (unlimited) a 9MB animated GIF download is never downsized because the guard requires `> 0`, then fails upload creation with a confusing size error.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb#create_upload`, the API URL download cap was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This is verifiable in the diff and means admins configuring `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB (or to 0/unlimited) will still have API URL downloads limited to 10MB, i.e., behavior no longer matches the setting. The additional downsizing loop is also gated by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`, reinforcing that the setting value is still intended to drive size behavior, making the hardcoded 10MB inconsistency a real defect. (The claim about a 9MB GIF failing when the setting is 0 is not directly supported by the shown diff.)
